group_assessment.group: A two-centre collaboration, 20 authors: the clinical-genetics half is M Koenig's (IGBMC Strasbourg / Montpellier, corresponding) with Mallaret and Synofzik as joint first authors and the Tübingen group (Schöls, Schüle, Bauer); the experimental half is the Aldaz laboratory at MD Anderson (Lee, Sagum, Bedford, Aldaz 19th), which supplies the GST-WW constructs, the peptide pull-down and the Wwox knock-out mouse. The Saudi and Israeli-Palestinian families come from Salih (Riyadh) and Mahajnah/Sharkia (Hadera/Kfar Qari').
group_assessment.research_type_note: 🔴 'mixed' is chosen from the closed vocabulary and it is not a hedge: the Methods contain two different evidence-producing machines under one author list. Exome sequencing, Sanger segregation and a 189-patient screen are descriptive_clinical run by a primary_disease_group; the GST constructs, the peptide pull-down, the homology model and the mouse are experimental_lab run by the gene-primary laboratory. Classifying the whole as either one would misweight half the paper.
group_assessment.total_publications_basis: `Koenig M[Author]` = 1020 on esearch, 2026-09-13 — the corresponding author's surname-initial query, and it is an UPPER BOUND rather than a career count: 'Koenig M' is a common author string and this query does not disambiguate homonyms. Recorded with that caveat because the field demands an integer and an undisambiguated integer presented as a career total is exactly the shape this repository has been bitten by. The disambiguated figure this reading actually leans on is the gene-specific one: `Koenig M[Author] AND WWOX` = 3 against `Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX` = 38, with `Aldaz CM[Author]` = 138 and `Koenig M[Author] AND (ataxia OR ataxias)` = 147.
group_assessment.primary_for_the_gene: The gene-primary laboratory is a CO-AUTHOR, not the lead: measured by esearch this session, `Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX` = 38 records against `Koenig M[Author] AND WWOX` = 3. Aldaz cloned WWOX; the mouse and the pull-down in this paper are his laboratory's instruments.
group_assessment.primary_for_the_disease: YES for the phenotype, and this is the separation that matters for weighting. Koenig's group is a primary group for autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia and had already localized THIS family's disease to 16q21-q23 (Gribaa 2007, resolved this session to PMID 17470496); the WWOX expertise is borrowed from the co-authoring gene laboratory. So the clinical observation is made by people primary for the disease, and the molecular assay by people primary for the gene — an unusually favourable split for the observation half.
group_assessment.weighting: 🔴 Observation and interpretation weigh differently, and the split runs along the authorship seam. The CLINICAL OBSERVATION (two consanguineous families, six affected individuals, segregation by Sanger, a 189-patient screen that found nothing further) is cohort work by a disease-primary group and is the strongest thing in the paper. The MOLECULAR INTERPRETATION is thinner than the clinical half and its instruments are borrowed: one in vitro peptide pull-down on bacterially expressed fusion proteins, one homology model, and a mouse that is a FULL Wwox knock-out rather than a model of either human variant. Every mechanistic sentence about what the variants do in a patient's brain is therefore an inference across systems, and the paper's own hedges ('presumably', 'most likely', 'suggesting') mark them. The abundance datum — the one the registry leans on — sits on the interpretation side and on a single individual.

entries.proposition: THE COHORT'S FIRST HALF, AND ITS PROVENANCE IS AN EARLIER PAPER: Family 1 is a large consanguineous Saudi family with four affected children, and this paper's own framing of it is a restatement of Gribaa 2007 (resolved this session to PMID 17470496), where the phenotype and the linkage interval were established.
entries.snippet: We reported a new form of childhood onset autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia with generalized tonic-clonic epilepsy and mental retardation in a large consanguineous family from Saudi Arabia with four affected children
entries.anchor: Introduction, final paragraph, first sentence
entries.abstract_snippet: We previously localized a new form of recessive ataxia with generalized tonic-clonic epilepsy and mental retardation to a 19 Mb interval in 16q21-q23 by homozygosity mapping of a large consanguineous Saudi Arabian family.

entries.proposition: VARIANT 1, AT RESIDUE AND DOMAIN LEVEL, from the paper's own text: p.Pro47Thr sits in the first WW domain and is a hydrophobic-to-polar substitution. This is the variant every downstream statement in this repository about 'the WW1 missense allele' descends from.
entries.snippet: The mutation affects the first WW domain (WW1) of WWOX (p.Pro47Thr) and causes a radical change from a hydrophobic amino acid, proline, to a polar one, threonine.
entries.anchor: Results, 'Mutation analysis of Family 1', second paragraph
entries.abstract_snippet: We now report the identification by whole exome sequencing of the missense mutation changing proline 47 into threonine in the first WW domain of the WW domain containing oxidoreductase gene,

entries.proposition: BOTH VARIANTS AT NUCLEOTIDE AND PROTEIN LEVEL, IN ONE ATTESTED SENTENCE, and it is the figure's own caption rather than the running text: c.139C>A / p.Pro47Thr in Family 1 and c.1114G>C / p.Gly372Arg in Family 2. Quoted from the caption deliberately — the running-text sentence carrying the second variant is split across an italic gene name in this surface, and a stitched quote is refused by this repository.
entries.snippet: Family trees showing consanguinity and segregation of the disease with mutations c.139C>A, causing the p.Pro47Thr missense change (47T) and c.1114G>C causing the p.Gly372Arg missense change (372R).
entries.anchor: Figure 1 caption, clause (A)
entries.abstract_snippet: We also identified another highly conserved homozygous WWOX mutation changing glycine 372 to arginine in a second consanguineous family.

entries.proposition: THE SEGREGATION EVIDENCE IS SANGER ON FOUR TRACES, NOT ON THE WHOLE PEDIGREE: in the PUBLISHED pedigrees of Mallaret et al., Brain 2014;137(Pt 2):411-419 (PMID 24369382 / PMCID PMC3914474 / DOI 10.1093/brain/awt338), Figure 1B sequences one index patient and one carrier parent per family — the two consanguineous families that paper reports, labelled Family 1 and Family 2 by its own authors. The genotypes of the other relatives are pedigree labels, which is a different kind of evidence from a printed trace. 🔴 ATTRIBUTION STATED IN THIS RECORD ON PURPOSE: the relatives named in the quoted caption below are members of that published cohort, identified exactly as the article identifies them, and they are no individual of any private overlay. The citation travels with the assertion rather than sitting in a neighbouring field.
entries.snippet: Sanger sequencing of the mutations c.139C>A and c.1114G>C: index patients are homozygous for the substitution and carrier relatives (mother I-2 in Family 1 and father I-1 in Family 2) are heterozygous for the same substitution.
entries.anchor: Figure 1 caption, clause (B)
entries.abstract_anchoring_waived: The abstract reports the variants and says nothing about which individuals were sequenced by which method.

entries.proposition: WHAT FAMILY 2 ADDS TO THE PHENOTYPE, AND IT IS AN EXPANSION RATHER THAN A REPLICATION: the same triad plus prominent upper motor neuron involvement, which the authors themselves read as spastic ataxia or complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia.
entries.snippet: In addition, prominent upper motor neuron affection with leg spasticity and positive bilateral extensor plantar response was present, thus resembling spastic ataxia or complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia.
entries.anchor: Results, 'Mutation analysis of Family 2'
entries.abstract_snippet: The phenotype closely resembled the index family, presenting with generalized tonic-clonic epilepsy, mental retardation and ataxia, but also included prominent upper motor neuron disease.

entries.proposition: THE PAPER'S OWN NEGATIVE, AND IT BOUNDS EVERY PREVALENCE STATEMENT BUILT ON THIS PAPER: a 189-patient, 182-family screen of the WWOX coding exons found no further mutation. The cohort is two families because the screen returned nothing, not because only two were looked for.
entries.snippet: in 189 unrelated ataxic patients with no molecular diagnosis (seven patients with childhood onset ataxia associated with epilepsy, 67 patients with onset of ataxia before 3 years, and 135 patients with onset of ataxia before 20 years) revealed no additional mutation.

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIGURE ATTESTATION THAT QUALIFIES THE PAPER'S ABSOLUTE NEGATIVE: in the pull-down panel the WWOX1-mutant lane is NOT blank. At 600 dpi it carries a faint, thin signal at the height of the wild-type WWOX1 band, far weaker than the wild-type lane but visibly above the background of the WWOX1-2-mutant lane, which is genuinely empty. 'Failed to interact' is therefore exact for the tandem construct and an overstatement for the WW1-only construct, where the honest reading is a strong reduction with residual binding. The direction of the result is unaffected; its absoluteness is.

entries.proposition: FIGURE ATTESTATION — THE CONSERVATION EVIDENCE, AND ITS ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE TWO VARIANTS: the alignment prints twelve species. At the P47 column every species carries P; at the G372 column the insect rows depart from the mammalian consensus, which is the paper's own stated exception. The conservation argument is therefore strong for P47 and weaker for G372, and that difference is visible on the panel rather than only in the caption.
